card.title: TYPE 4 Ho-Ro
card.flavorText: The Type 4 Ho-Ro was a self-propelled gun developed and used by the Imperial Japanese Army in WWII. It was inspired by the German Grille series of self-propelled artillery and had a Type 38 150 mm howitzer mounted on a tracked chassis of a slightly modified Type 97 Chi-Ha chassis. The Type 4 Ho-Ro had a crew of 6 and a maximum rate of fire of only 5 rounds per minute. Only a handful of them were produced (approx. 12 units) and only one of them was captured by the Allies at Luzon and is now preserved at the United States Marine Corps Museum in Quantico, Virginia.
